title: Segment the T-Rex skull into rings from the seamless parametrization: small iso-line loops that cut the mesh (teeth bases, jaw hinge), crease-conforming lines and cones
user-messages: [recalled] I want another agent  looking at how to segment (create rings in the ring tool) the skull using the seamless parameterization, and the singular points, somthing along the lines of using the parameterization lines that conform to the mesh where there are highpoints in the crease field and where there are small loops in the parameterization that cut the mesh like at the base of the teeth or at the jaw hinge that is what we are looking for
description:
Segment the T-Rex skull into rings in the ring tool (spline_ring / spline_cut / add_label, crease mode where it helps) by reading the quad-layout pipeline's seamless parametrization and its cones, instead of fitting rings from scratch. The user's idea: the parametrization's iso-lines that conform to the mesh where the crease field is high are candidate ring paths, and small closed loops of the parametrization that cut the mesh, at the base of each tooth or around the jaw hinge, are exactly the cuts a segmentation wants. Cones (singular points) mark extrema and saddles and seed or bound those loops (see the CRAW-112 note about cones as ring seeds).

Before designing anything, study what has not worked: the craw-112-fable branch (origin/craw-112-fable in the Ixdar repo, an earlier ring-fit attempt) and ai-workspace/ring_fit_failed_approaches.md, the user's log of failed ring-fit approaches. The crawfish scans have examples of good segmentations: ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/crawfish/IMG_41xx.dsl over the scans in ${IXDAR_DATA_ROOT}/crawfish/IMG_41xx.glb (the data root defaults to the home folder); use them to judge what a good ring looks like and as test cases.

Inputs available on master: every model scene opens a DSL (CRAW-126), param-exam shows the skull's seamless iso-lines and cones, the skull DSL is load_mesh + repair_mesh + quad_layout over the Trellis GLB, and ComfyUI P3-SAM part labels can seed rings (CRAW-125) as a comparison.

## Failed approaches and how this avoids them (CRAW-129 agent, 2026-11-22)

Every entry in ring_fit_failed_approaches.md (F1-F27) and the craw-112-fable branch (RegionClusterFit, SurfaceLifetime air flow, RestingSphere walls; 13-14 of 20 bench cases at best) moves rings already drawn into grooves by descending an energy. They fail on: picked weights between aims (C1), crease thresholds deciding what a groove or wall is (F16, F19, F25-F27), rings owning grooves (C2/C3), flat energy away from grooves (C4), steppers that stall (C5), creases that attract and so cannot tell a pit from a groove (F22-F25), and ratios with no shared scale (C6).

This ticket does not fit drawn rings. It enumerates every closed iso-line of the seamless map and so needs no descent (C4, C5 gone). A loop exists only where an iso-line closes round a part or a handle, so a pit cannot make one (F27's "a wall is a band round something"). Crease enters only as an argmax inside one family of parallel loops, so its scale and any threshold never matter (C1, F19). Nothing is assigned: each family proposes at most one ring (C2, C3). Families are ranked by one dimensionless quantity, L^2 / (4 pi A_small) (C6). It does not replace the fit for the artist's drawn rings (requirements 4, 7-9 do not apply).

## Design (as built)

1. IsoLineLoops (quadlayout.seamless): traces u = c / v = c face to face; the quarter turns across an edge are read from the edge's direction in the two charts' corner UVs, an odd turn swaps the coordinate. A trace is a loop when it re-enters a face in the same direction on the same coordinate (closes within one face). Gives up on folds, boundaries, cone faces, or past sqrt(2 pi A) (isoperimetric bound). Every untouched (face, coordinate) lane seeds one trace (Jobard-Lefer coverage).
2. IsoLoopRings (rings): per loop, a two-sided flood from its strip: separating or not, small side area and cones. Family = same small-side cone set (a disc bounded by a closed iso-line holds cones of index sum +1, Poincare-Hopf; measured: every tooth loop has index4 sum 4); handle loops join when their strips neighbour on one iso direction. Per family the loop of highest mean valley curvature; families taken by neck ratio, skipping any loop within one face of a kept one; part labels at the deepest face of each cut-off region, plus body.
3. Node iso_loop_rings(geometry, field=layout.field, seamless=layout.seamless): ring_NN marks + labels + report. Ring tool ctrl+shift+K keep-graph-rings marks them for saving (crease mode where the ring's mean crease strength beats the surface mean); the save drops the proposal and its quad_layout statement.
definition-of-done:
1. The failed approaches in ring_fit_failed_approaches.md and on craw-112-fable are summarised on the ticket, with how this approach avoids each.
2. A method (DSL node and/or ring-tool command) that proposes rings from the seamless parametrization: closed iso-line loops that cut the mesh, ranked by crease strength along them and by loop length, with cones used as described in the design.
3. On the T-Rex skull it proposes rings at the base of the teeth and around the jaw hinge, written as a ring DSL that reloads in the ring scene, with screenshots under tmp/.
4. On at least two crawfish scans it is compared against their existing good segmentations (which existing rings it recovers, which it misses, which it adds), reported with screenshots.
5. Build checkstyle-green; tests cover the loop extraction on a small fixture.
testing-plan: 1. Skull: proposed rings in the ring scene, screenshots. 2. Two crawfish scans: compare to their existing ring DSLs. 3. Unit test on a torus or capsule fixture.
unknowns: Crawfish comparison blocked: quad_layout refuses every crawfish scan tried (IMG_4110, 4111, 4112) as pleated: repair_mesh's unfold leaves 1 to 23 folded faces (stillFolded), a second repair_mesh pass leaves 1-2, Taubin smoothing makes it worse (8). Needs repair_mesh to unfold completely (separate ticket) before DoD 4 can run.

Tooth rings sit where the teeth part from their neighbours, not at the gum groove: on this Trellis mesh the teeth fuse near the gum, so a loop round one tooth ends above the fusion and the gum groove belongs to loops round tooth groups. Options: keep (honest to the parametrization), or pick each separating family's outermost loop instead of its deepest crease.
changes-made: IsoLineLoops: closed iso-line loops of a seamless parametrization, traced across its quarter-turn transitions

IsoLoopRings: loop sides and cones, families by small-side cone set or neighbouring handle strips, deepest-groove loop per family, ranking by L^2/(4 pi A_small), non-crossing selection, part labels, mapping onto the ring surface
iso_loop_rings node; ring tool keep-graph-rings (ctrl+shift+K); RingDslWriter.withoutProposals so a save drops the proposal and its layout
Skull: 1710 closed loops, 80 families, 78 rings (31 round handles, 47 separating, nearly all teeth with index4 sum 4); reloads from ~/.ix/ixdar-models/dsl/trex_skull_iso_rings.dsl in 4 s

Saddle cuts: IsoLineLoops.traceSeparatrices and crossFace; StripSides (the two-sided flood, now shared by rings and cuts); IsoLoopBisectors (two separatrices of one saddle that end on rings and cut their region, ratio L^2/(4 pi A_small) below one, one per saddle, greedy); the node puts them on the bundle and keep-graph-rings turns them into spline_cut bisectors after re-tracing the rings from their anchors

Skull rings + cuts: 600 saddles, 52 cuts proposed, 42 traced; 66 -> 109 regions, slivers 3 -> 25 (22 are pockets at a cut's end on its ring), rings splitting nothing 6 -> 1; left mandible separated from chin and articulation; fused tooth groups still not separated. ~/.ix/ixdar-models/dsl/trex_skull_iso_cuts.dsl, launch entry 'CRAW-129: skull rings and saddle cuts'

iso_loop_rings pick port: crease (default) or outermost (each separating family keeps the loop with most surface on its smaller side). Skull outermost with cuts: 111 regions (84 non-sliver), 27 slivers, 1 ring splitting nothing; teeth cut at the gum line; fused groups still not separated. ~/.ix/ixdar-models/dsl/trex_skull_iso_outermost.dsl
